q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT DISTINCT v1.bar, v2.bar FROM serves AS v1, serves AS v2 WHERE v1.beer IN (v2.beer) AND v1.bar <> v2.bar

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they are checking for different conditions. Q1 is looking for bars that serve a beer which no other bar serves, and Q2 is looking for bars that serve a beer which at least one other bar also serves.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two bars, 'Bar A' and 'Bar B', and at least two beers, 'Beer X' and 'Beer Y'. 'Bar A' should serve 'Beer X' and 'Beer Y', while 'Bar B' should only serve 'Beer X'. This setup triggers the difference because 'Bar A' will be included in Q1's result as it serves a beer ('Beer X') that no other bar serves, but 'Bar A' will not be included in Q2's result as 'Beer X' is also served by 'Bar B'.
